prompt: Resonance in an open pipe with a tuning fork: how does the end correction e relate to two successive resonance lengths?
explain: Successive resonances differ by λ/2, so λ = 2(L₂ − L₁), and the end correction cancels out.
subject: Physics

prompt: Absolute temperature of air in an open pipe is made 4 times. Its fundamental frequency becomes (expansion ignored)?
explain: f = v/2L and v ∝ √T, so quadrupling T doubles the frequency.
subject: Physics

prompt: Loading a tuning fork prong with a little wax changes its frequency how?
explain: Wax adds mass to the prong, so the fork vibrates more slowly and its frequency decreases.
subject: Physics

prompt: Filing the prong of a tuning fork changes its frequency how?
explain: Filing removes mass from the prong, so the frequency increases.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two waves of equal amplitude A form beats. The maximum resultant amplitude is?
explain: At a beat maximum the waves are in phase, so the amplitudes add to 2A.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two sources each of intensity I₀ produce beats. Intensity at the point varies between?
explain: A_max = 2A gives 4I₀, and equal amplitudes give A_min = 0.
subject: Physics

prompt: Beats can be distinctly heard by the ear only if the frequency difference is at most about?
explain: The ear resolves waxing and waning of sound only up to about 10 beats per second.
subject: Physics

prompt: An unknown fork is loaded with wax and its beats with a standard fork decrease. The unknown fork is?
options: Of higher frequency than the standard
Of lower frequency than the standard
explain: Wax lowers its frequency. Beats decrease only if it was above the standard, so it moves closer.
subject: Physics

prompt: An unknown fork is filed and its beats with a standard fork decrease. The unknown fork was?
options: Lower in frequency than the standard
Higher in frequency than the standard
explain: Filing raises its frequency. Beats fall only if it moves toward the standard from below.
subject: Physics

prompt: Beats arise from superposition of waves that differ slightly in what, giving interference in time?
explain: Slightly different frequencies shift the phase with time, so intensity at a point alternates with time.
subject: Physics

prompt: Waves y₁ = A sin(2π·100t) and y₂ = A sin(2π·104t) superpose. Number of beats per second is?
explain: Frequencies are 100 Hz and 104 Hz, so beat frequency = 104 − 100 = 4 Hz.
subject: Physics

prompt: A wave has period T. Two points λ/2 apart differ in time of oscillation by?
explain: Phase difference π corresponds to time lag T/2.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: An upward pulse moves right on a string. A particle on its leading (front) edge moves in which direction?
options: Along the string, to the right
explain: Front edge has negative slope, so vₚ = −v(slope) > 0: the particle moves up as the pulse arrives.
subject: Physics
topic: Particle velocity & acceleration vs wave speed

prompt: For y = A sin(ωt − kx), at a particle's mean position, which is true?
explain: At y = 0: a = −ω²y = 0, and speed = ω√(A²−y²) is maximum (Aω).
subject: Physics
topic: Particle velocity & acceleration vs wave speed

prompt: A block hangs from a string in a lift accelerating upward. Transverse wave speed on the string, compared to rest?
explain: Tension rises to m(g + a), so v = √(T/μ) increases.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: Two wires of the same material, different radii, carry the same tensile stress. Their transverse wave speeds are?
explain: T/μ = (σA)/(ρA) = σ/ρ, so v depends only on stress and density, not on the area.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: In air, the speed of sound at constant temperature, when the pressure is doubled (density also doubles), becomes:
explain: P/ρ stays constant at constant T (Boyle's law), so v = √(γP/ρ) is unchanged.
subject: Physics
topic: Effect of temperature, pressure on sound speed

prompt: At the same temperature, v(H₂)/v(O₂) in sound speed is (both diatomic, ideal)?
explain: Same γ and T, so v ∝ 1/√M. M(O₂)/M(H₂) = 16, so the ratio is √16 = 4.
subject: Physics
topic: Effect of temperature, pressure on sound speed

prompt: In beats, the resultant sound has a frequency equal to which quantity?
explain: The carrier (heard pitch) is the mean frequency (f₁+f₂)/2; its amplitude varies at f₁−f₂.
subject: Physics

prompt: For beats from equal-amplitude waves, the amplitude envelope has frequency ___ the beat frequency.
explain: |cos(π Δf t)| repeats at Δf, so the amplitude envelope has the same frequency as the beats (intensity maxima).
subject: Physics

prompt: A source sounding f and its reflection from a receding wall give beats. Beats arise due to what?
options: Doppler shift in the reflected wave
Phase change of π on reflection
Change in wave speed in air
explain: The reflected wave has a Doppler-shifted frequency; its slight difference from f produces beats.
subject: Physics

prompt: A sinusoidal wave of fixed f and A runs on a string. Tension is made 4 times. Power transmitted becomes?
explain: P = ½μω²A²v and v ∝ √T, so P ∝ √T. Quadrupling T doubles P.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: A uniform heavy rope hangs from a ceiling. A transverse pulse on it has the greatest speed at which place?
options: At the top, near the ceiling
explain: Tension at distance x from the free end is μgx, so v = √(gx) is largest at the top.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: A source of fixed frequency drives a string. Tension is made 4 times. The wavelength on the string becomes?
explain: f is fixed by the source and v ∝ √T, so λ ∝ √T. Quadrupling T doubles λ.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: Two waves of amplitudes in ratio 3:1 produce beats. Ratio I_max : I_min is?
explain: Amplitudes 3 and 1 give (3+1)²/(3−1)² = 16/4 = 4 : 1.
subject: Physics

prompt: A sonometer wire beats with a fork. Raising the wire tension increases the beats. The wire was?
options: Higher in frequency than the fork
Lower in frequency than the fork
Equal in frequency to the fork
explain: Higher tension raises the wire frequency. Beats increase only if the wire was already above the fork.
subject: Physics

prompt: A sine wave travels on a string. Which quantity is independent of the wave's amplitude?
explain: Wave speed depends only on T and μ; particle speed (ωA), acceleration and energy all depend on A.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: A uniform heavy rope hangs vertically. Pulse speed at distance x above its free lower end is?
explain: Tension at height x supports the rope length x below it: T = μgx, so v = √(gx).
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: Which medium can support both transverse and longitudinal mechanical waves?
explain: Solids have both bulk and shear modulus, so they carry both wave types; gases and bulk liquids carry only longitudinal.
subject: Physics

prompt: In a longitudinal wave, the wavelength is the distance between two successive:
options: Compression and the second next compression
explain: Compressions play the role of crests, so λ is the distance between successive compressions (or successive rarefactions).
subject: Physics

prompt: A wave is y = sin(2x − 6t) in SI units. Its speed is?
explain: v = ω/k = 6/2 = 3 m/s, moving along +x.
subject: Physics

prompt: Average energy per unit volume in a progressive wave in a medium of density ρ is?
explain: Energy density u = ½ρω²A², with equal KE and PE averages. Intensity I = u·v.
subject: Physics

prompt: Instantaneous power carried by a string wave is maximum when the element's displacement is?
explain: KE and PE of an element are in phase and both are maximum at y = 0, so energy flow is greatest there.
subject: Physics

prompt: Phase difference between y = A sin(kx − ωt) and y = A sin(ωt − kx)?
explain: sin(kx − ωt) = −sin(ωt − kx), so the two waves are exactly opposite in phase.
subject: Physics

prompt: A wave is y = 0.5 sin(4πx − 200πt) in SI units. Its frequency is?
explain: ω = 200π gives f = ω/2π = 100 Hz.
subject: Physics

prompt: A wave is y = 3 sin(4x − 8t) in SI units. Its wavelength is?
explain: k = 4 rad/m, so λ = 2π/k = π/2 m.
subject: Physics

prompt: For y = A sin(20πt − 4πx) in SI units, the wave speed is?
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: For a non-dispersive wave, the graph of ω versus k is a straight line whose slope gives?
explain: ω = vk passes through the origin, and its slope is the wave speed v.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: In y = A sin(ωt − kx), a particle farther along +x oscillates with phase that:
options: Leads that of one at smaller x
Lags behind that of one at smaller x
explain: The wave reaches larger x later, so those particles lag in phase by kΔx.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: In a travelling harmonic wave, particle velocity compared with particle displacement is in phase:
explain: v_p ∝ cos(ωt−kx) while y ∝ sin(ωt−kx), so velocity leads displacement by π/2.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: The same wave travels in the same medium and its frequency is doubled. Its angular wave number k:
explain: v is fixed, so λ halves and k = 2π/λ doubles.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: Two points on a progressive wave oscillate in the same phase when their separation is?
explain: Δφ = 2πn requires a path difference Δx = nλ.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: The number of complete waves per unit length (spectroscopic wave number) equals?
explain: Spectroscopic wave number = 1/λ, while angular wave number k = 2π/λ.
subject: Physics
topic: Wave parameters: k, ω, λ, f, phase relations

prompt: Source frequency is doubled at the same amplitude on a string at fixed tension. What happens?
options: v unchanged; max particle speed doubles
v doubles; max particle speed doubles
v doubles; max particle speed unchanged
explain: v = √(T/μ) is set by the medium; vₚ,max = Aω is proportional to f, so it doubles.
subject: Physics
topic: Particle velocity & acceleration vs wave speed

prompt: In a harmonic wave, the graph of particle velocity vₚ against its displacement y is a/an:
explain: vₚ = ±ω√(A²−y²) gives vₚ²/(Aω)² + y²/A² = 1, an ellipse.
subject: Physics
topic: Particle velocity & acceleration vs wave speed

prompt: In a sound wave, pressure amplitude Δp₀ in terms of density ρ, wave speed v, particle velocity amplitude u₀?
explain: Δp₀ = Bk s₀ = ρv²(ω/v)s₀ = ρ v (ω s₀) = ρ v u₀.
subject: Physics
topic: Particle velocity & acceleration vs wave speed

prompt: A wire of density ρ, Young's modulus Y is stretched with small strain ε. Transverse wave speed is?
explain: v = √(T/μ) = √(YAε/ρA) = √(Yε/ρ), which is less than the longitudinal speed √(Y/ρ).
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: A pulse on a stretched string is made narrower, with the same tension. Its speed?
options: Doubles if the width is halved
explain: Speed depends only on T and μ, not on pulse shape or width (non-dispersive).
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: Two transverse pulses travel in opposite directions on the same string and cross. Each pulse's speed is?
options: Zero at the instant of overlap
explain: Speed depends only on T and μ of the string. Pulses superpose and pass through each other unchanged.
subject: Physics
topic: Speed of transverse wave on string √(T/μ)

prompt: A gas in a rigid closed vessel is heated so that its pressure becomes 4 times. Speed of sound becomes?
explain: Rigid vessel keeps ρ fixed, so v ∝ √P; with P×4, v doubles.
subject: Physics
topic: Effect of temperature, pressure on sound speed

prompt: Absolute temperature of air rises by a small 2%. Speed of sound rises by about?
explain: Since v ∝ √T, the fractional change in v is half that in T, so 1%.
subject: Physics
topic: Effect of temperature, pressure on sound speed

prompt: In the troposphere, speed of sound falls with height mainly because which quantity falls?
explain: v ∝ √T. Pressure alone does not affect v, as P and ρ fall together and P/ρ stays constant at fixed T.
subject: Physics
topic: Effect of temperature, pressure on sound speed

prompt: Air at constant pressure is heated until its density becomes 1/4 of the original. Speed of sound becomes:
explain: At constant P, v ∝ 1/√ρ, so a density of 1/4 gives v doubled.
subject: Physics
topic: Effect of temperature, pressure on sound speed

prompt: Two waves of equal amplitude A differ in phase by 120°. Resultant amplitude is?
explain: 2A cos 60° = A.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two equal and opposite pulses on a string overlap completely. At that instant the string's energy is?
explain: The displacement is zero everywhere, so potential energy is zero. The particles still move, so the energy is kinetic.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two coherent sources vibrate in antiphase. At a point equidistant from both, the interference is?
explain: The path difference is zero, but the source phase difference of π gives destructive interference.
subject: Physics

prompt: In interference, the energy 'missing' at destructive points is?
explain: Energy is conserved; it is redistributed, and the average intensity is unchanged.
subject: Physics

prompt: The simple principle of superposition (y = y₁ + y₂) strictly holds for waves in which medium?
explain: It follows from the linear wave equation, so it applies to small-amplitude waves in a linear medium.
subject: Physics

prompt: Equal-amplitude waves A sin ωt and A sin(ωt+φ) superpose. Resultant's initial phase (w.r.t. first) is?
explain: Sum-to-product gives 2A cos(φ/2) sin(ωt+φ/2), so the resultant leads the first wave by φ/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: String fixed at both ends: frequencies of 1st, 2nd, 3rd overtones are in the ratio?
explain: The overtones are the 2nd, 3rd and 4th harmonics, so the ratio is 2 : 3 : 4.
subject: Physics

prompt: A string fixed at both ends is plucked at one-third of its length. Which harmonic is missing?
explain: A node at L/3 is not possible for harmonics having a node there. The 3rd (and its multiples) has a node at L/3.
subject: Physics

prompt: String fixed at one end, free at the other, vibrates at 5 times its fundamental. Number of antinodes?
explain: Frequencies f, 3f, 5f have 1, 2, 3 antinodes respectively (the free end is an antinode).
subject: Physics

prompt: A string driven at fixed frequency shows 4 loops. Tension is made 4 times (same L). Number of loops?
explain: v doubles, so λ doubles, and the loops (= 2L/λ) halve to 2.
subject: Physics

prompt: String of length L fixed at both ends in 3rd harmonic: nearest node to an end (other than the end) is at?
explain: The nodes are spaced λ/2 = L/3 apart, so they lie at L/3 and 2L/3.
subject: Physics

prompt: A vibrating string sets the surrounding air into vibration. Which quantity is the same for string wave and sound?
explain: The forced air vibrates at the source frequency; speed and wavelength differ.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a string fixed at both ends, standing wave y = a sin(kx) cos(ωt) in the nth mode requires k = ?
explain: sin(kL) = 0 gives kL = nπ, so k = nπ/L (equivalent to λ = 2L/n).
subject: Physics

prompt: In Melde's experiment, with the fork vibrating along the string's length, the string's frequency is?
explain: In the longitudinal arrangement the string completes one cycle for every two fork vibrations: f_string = f_fork/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: The quality (timbre) of a note from a string depends on which feature?
options: Number and relative strength of harmonics
explain: Timbre is fixed by which overtones are present and their relative intensities.
subject: Physics

prompt: Third harmonic of a string fixed at both ends is 300 Hz. Frequency of its first overtone?
explain: f₁ = 100 Hz. The first overtone is the 2nd harmonic = 200 Hz.
subject: Physics

prompt: For small vibrations, increasing the amplitude of a string's vibration changes its fundamental frequency how?
explain: The frequency depends on L, T and μ only, not on amplitude.
subject: Physics

prompt: A vibrating string fixed at both ends is touched lightly at its midpoint. Which harmonics can persist?
explain: Touching imposes a node at the centre. Only even harmonics have a node at L/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a string fixed at both ends, the period of the fundamental mode equals the time taken by a pulse to?
explain: f₁ = v/2L, so the period 2L/v equals the round-trip time of a pulse.
subject: Physics

prompt: Same L, T, μ: ratio of fundamental of a fixed-free string to that of a fixed-fixed string?
explain: Fixed–free gives λ = 4L, fixed–fixed gives λ = 2L, so the frequency ratio is 1 : 2.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two successive resonances of a string fixed at both ends have frequency ratio 4 : 5. They are which harmonics?
explain: fₙ ∝ n, so consecutive harmonics in the ratio 4 : 5 are the 4th and 5th.
subject: Physics

prompt: Closed pipe of length L: wavelength of its 5th harmonic is?
explain: L = 5λ/4 for the 5th harmonic, so λ = 4L/5.
subject: Physics

prompt: Closed pipe of length L in 3rd harmonic: nearest displacement node to the open end is at distance?
formula: λ = 4L/3, node at λ/4 from open end
explain: λ = 4L/3; the first node from the open end lies λ/4 = L/3 away.
subject: Physics

prompt: A closed pipe is filled with a gas of same γ and T but 4× the molar mass. Its fundamental frequency?
explain: v ∝ 1/√M, so v halves; L is fixed, so f halves.
subject: Physics

prompt: Water is slowly poured into a tube closed at the bottom with a fork sounding. Fundamental of the air column?
explain: Air column length L decreases, so f = v/4L increases.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a closed pipe of length L, the gap between successive resonant frequencies is?
explain: Successive odd harmonics differ by 2f₁ = 2·(v/4L) = v/2L.
subject: Physics

prompt: An open pipe vibrates in its 3rd harmonic. How many displacement nodes lie inside the pipe?
explain: nth harmonic of an open pipe has n displacement nodes inside and n+1 antinodes (ends included).
subject: Physics

prompt: An open pipe is cut into two equal halves. The fundamental frequency of each half compared with the original is?
explain: f ∝ 1/L for an open pipe, so halving the length doubles the fundamental.
subject: Physics

prompt: A closed pipe has the same fundamental as an open pipe of length L. Its length is?
explain: v/4L′ = v/2L gives L′ = L/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: For an open pipe of fixed length, increasing its radius makes the fundamental frequency?
explain: Larger r gives a larger end correction, so the effective length grows and f falls.
subject: Physics

prompt: y₁ = A sin ω₁t and y₂ = A sin ω₂t superpose. The beat frequency in Hz is?
explain: Beat frequency = f₁ − f₂, and f = ω/2π, so f_beat = (ω₁ − ω₂)/2π.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two nearby sources of slightly different frequencies produce beats. At different points in the room, the beat rate is?
options: Zero at points of equal path
explain: Beat frequency is f₁ − f₂ everywhere; position only shifts the phase and the loudness.
subject: Physics

prompt: The second harmonic of a 256 Hz source is sounded with a 510 Hz source. Beats per second?
explain: The second harmonic is 512 Hz, and 512 − 510 = 2 beats/s.
subject: Physics
